task: The people team pulls payroll and org-chart numbers out of the HR system by hand each quarter, and they never match. Titles are typed five ways, one reporting line goes round in a circle, and the salary history has copies and rows dated before people were hired. Build a pipeline that cleans the employee records, maps every reporting line, ranks salaries as of 31 March 2026, and publishes the department payroll with a summary that accounts for every employee.
problems: Job titles in the wrong case or with extra spaces; emails with capitals; phone numbers in five formats.
One manager loop: a team manager's manager is one of their own reports, so neither chain reaches the chief executive.
Three salary history rows repeated exactly.
Two salary history rows dated before the employee's hire date.
Salaries are multiples of 2,500, so many people in a department earn the same amount.
Some people marked terminated left after the payroll date, and the employee table's salary already includes April's raises.
revenue: Payroll is reported as of 31 March 2026. A person is on it when they were hired on or before that day, hadn't left by it, and have a salary history row dated between their hire date and that day; their salary is the latest such row. Rankings are within each department, highest salary first: equal salaries share a rank, and positions break ties by earlier hire date, then employee id.
